unresolved_should_improve.claim: The revision keeps the statement that intensity offers no basis for a ratio. It deletes the provisional assumption ('for convenience') that the volume ratio may serve temporarily for intensity. It also deletes the closing 'he must stop there', which grounds p6's 'Thus, taking the year 1900'.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: The plan allows the intensity discussion to be compressed, and the essential points (intensity hard to measure, radiation, conservative ratio) survive.

evidence.quote: one might assume, for convenience, that the ten-year ratio for volume could be used temporarily for intensity
Unless the calculator was prepared to be instantly overwhelmed by physical force and mental complexity, he must stop there.
since he could get no basis for a ratio there. Within ten years a new universe of force had been revealed in radiation. At all events, the ten-year ratio seemed carefully conservative.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: After 'no basis for a ratio there', restore 'one might assume, for convenience, that the ten-year ratio for volume could be used temporarily for intensity'. Optionally restore the final 'he must stop there' sentence.
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: optional tradeoff, but compression left a dangling step
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The argument names a difficulty and never answers it, so 'At all events' concedes to nothing. The hedged, improvised method that defines the chapter's voice is lost.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Intensity problem raised then abandoned; 'must stop there' cut

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The revision cuts 'Any other formula would do as well … but this happens to be simple and convenient'. It also cuts the comet's 'For convenience, the most familiar image should come first', leaving 'The simplest figure' with no comparison.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: 'for convenience' itself survives in p8, so the required hedge is technically kept.

evidence.quote: Any other formula would do as well, either of chemical explosion, or electrolysis, or vegetable growth
Any other formula would do as well, either of chemical explosion, or electrolysis, or vegetable growth; but this happens to be simple and convenient.
Or better, one might, for convenience, use the formula of squares to serve for a law of mind. As the human meteoroid approached
The simplest figure is that of a perfect comet--say that of 1843--which drops from space

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore the first draft's 'Any other formula would do as well … but this happens to be simple and convenient.'
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The law of squares reads as more asserted than Adams allows. The continuity check asks that the 'for convenience' hedge be kept, and this sentence is its point.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Arbitrariness of the squares formula and comet framing lost

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The first draft already dropped the stationary-consumption sentence, leaving 'this stationary period' without its antecedent. The revision further cuts the generations dying in that faith, 'This mental inertia of science', and the authorities' continued resistance.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: Radium and inexhaustible force survive, so the factual turn is clear.

evidence.quote: the habit remains of founding statistics on the faith that consumption will continue nearly stationary
This mental inertia of science lasted through the eighties before showing signs of breaking up
This mental inertia of science lasted through the eighties before showing signs of breaking up
talked of this stationary period, which was to follow the explosion of new power. Nothing short of radium fairly wakened men

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Change 'this' to 'a' or restore the 'consumption will continue nearly stationary' clause. Prefix the radium sentence with 'This mental inertia of science lasted through the eighties; and'.
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: essential ('stationary period faith … broken only by radium')
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The chapter's inertia law ('inertia almost invariably has ended in tragedy') is no longer turned against science itself. The irony that the scientists were the inert mass breaks, and the Mill reference floats.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Science's own 'mental inertia' cut; 'this stationary period' unanchored

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The revision deletes 'They had reduced themselves to motion in a universe of motions … vertiginous violence', which the first draft kept. It also recasts away 'In 1850, science would have smiled at such a romance as this'.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: The comet, explosive, vegetable and saurian sequence and the 1850 line survive intact.

evidence.quote: They had reduced themselves to motion in a universe of motions, with an acceleration, in their own case of vertiginous violence.
In 1850, science would have smiled at such a romance as this, but, in 1900, few men of science thought it a laughing matter.
an order they had themselves disproved. If any analogy whatever existed between the human mind and the laws of motion

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Reinsert the single 'They had reduced themselves to motion…' sentence before 'If any analogy'.
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The leap to 'If any analogy whatever existed between the human mind and the laws of motion' loses its trigger. The 1850/1900 frame that closes on 'An average mind had succumbed already in 1850' is weakened.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Bridge from scientists-as-motion to the mind-as-comet analogy cut

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The revision cuts 'He had never been able to acquire knowledge, still less to impart it' and the nineteenth/twentieth-century American contrast. It also cuts 'a teacher who had failed to educate even the generation of 1870, dared not interfere', and the 'groaned and shrieked and shuddered' cadence.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: The timid Paris gentleman (V5) and 'promised to be docile, for once' preserve some self-irony.

evidence.quote: He had never been able to acquire knowledge, still less to impart it
a teacher who had failed to educate even the generation of 1870, dared not interfere
With that, a teacher who had failed to educate even the generation of 1870, dared not interfere.
Meanwhile he was getting education. The new forces would educate.
For the American of the twentieth century, a historian asked no longer to be teacher or even friend

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore the first draft's 'He had never been able to acquire knowledge…' sentence in p17 and the 1870 teacher sentence in p18.
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: Claims of ignorance set against sweeping prophecy are the voice profile's core device. Without them the pupil's docility toward 'a sort of God' reads as plain assertion rather than ironic self-portrait.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Historian's self-deprecation and failed-teacher irony removed

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The revision deletes 'As though thought were common salt in indefinite solution it must enter a new phase subject to new laws'. It also deletes the warning that the coming education 'promised to be violently coercive'.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: V8 and the unity-to-multiplicity sentence survive, so the conclusion still lands.

evidence.quote: As though thought were common salt in indefinite solution it must enter a new phase subject to new laws.
its style of education promised to be violently coercive

unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: essential ('the mind must jump'); the image is a planning gap not flagged
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The closing 'jump' loses its physical meaning as a discontinuous phase change. The ending moves from 'new social mind' to the jump without the image that makes the leap concrete.
